designs.title: Pisa
designs.why: Clean, confident one-ink line work: the perforated edge, double frame, spaced serif PISA and the postmark breaking out of the frame all read instantly as a stamp, and the 3.97° denomination doubling as the real lean is a smart insider wink. The tower drawing is accurate and well built (arcades, belfry arches, diamond inlays on the base). Weak points: the arcade bands are so dense and hairline that from 3 m they collapse into a grey stripe texture, and on the black tee the white thin lines risk gaining and plugging; the lower right of the stamp is empty while the postmark crowds the top right; overall it leans toward souvenir-shop polish more than a lived-in, worn stamp.
designs.fix: Simplify and thicken the tower's interior line work (fewer column lines per gallery, heavier arch strokes, a consistent minimum stroke of ~1 pt at print size) so each tier reads as a distinct band from a distance and holds up in white ink on black.
